plan.story:
Little Red Riding Hood skipped along the woodland path, carrying cake and a drink for Grandmother.

A wolf stepped from the ferns. “Where are you going?” he asked sweetly.

“To Grandmother’s cottage,” Red replied.

“Then take her some flowers!” suggested the wolf. While Red picked daisies, he hurried away.

At the cottage, he knocked and pretended to be Red. Grandmother opened the door. Gulp! He swallowed her whole, leaving her nightcap behind. He pulled it over his ears and climbed beneath the quilt.

Soon Red arrived. She set down her basket and approached the bed.

“Grandmother, what big ears you have!”

“All the better to hear you with.”

“What big eyes you have!”

“All the better to see you with.”

Red gripped her cape. “What big teeth you have!”

“All the better to eat you with!”

The wolf sprang. Red stumbled toward the door, eyes wide with fear—but he swallowed her whole. Then he fell asleep, snoring loudly.

A passing huntsman heard the dreadful noise and entered. Seeing the swollen wolf, he fetched scissors from the sewing table and carefully snipped open his belly.

Red scrambled out, trembling. Grandmother followed, and they hugged tightly, tears shining on their cheeks.

While the wolf slept, Red and the huntsman brought heavy stones from outside. They filled his belly, and Grandmother stitched it closed. He woke, tried to leap away, and collapsed dead beneath their weight.

Safe beside Grandmother, Red whispered, “Next time, I’ll stay on the path—and never trust a stranger’s smile.”
